<!--
Keep this comment, and never use a colon anywhere in it. The status page reads
the first comment of the body as key-value data and shows an error page for
this incident if a line ends in a colon or the body is empty.

The status page shows only this issue's TITLE and its COMMENTS, not this body.
The repo is public, so keep employee data and internal details out of all three.

To publish (full steps in README.md, section "Post an incident")
1. The title is what users see, e.g. "Payroll dispatch degraded". Include the
   lowercase word "degraded" for a partial problem (amber). Any other title
   shows as an outage (red).
2. After submitting, add the `status` label. That label is what puts the
   issue on the page. Do not add `simple-hq` or `simple-hq-legacy`.
3. Lock the conversation, so only maintainers can post updates.
4. Post the first public update as a comment.

This template deliberately applies no labels. GitHub applies template labels
for anyone who opens an issue, so `status` here would let strangers post
incidents on the public page.
-->
